models.collectorNote: Air-cooled parts cross over with the motorcycle world; the Sport Prinz's Bertone body is the collector's target and its rust the usual tax.

generations.name: Prinz I–III / Sport Prinz
generations.note: The twin made 20 hp at launch and 30 in the Sport Prinz; the engine was a enlarged motorcycle unit, and revved like one.

generations.name: Prinz 4
generations.note: The Prinz 4's styling quoted the Chevrolet Corvair in miniature; over 570,000 were built, the marque's volume backbone.

models.intro: NSU's return to cars: a rear-engined two-cylinder runabout that grew, in the Prinz 4 of 1961, into the sharp-edged 'bathtub' saloon half of Germany learned to drive in. The Sport Prinz coupé (Bertone, styled by Franco Scaglione) proved the little chassis had glamour in it.

models.collectorNote: TTS originality is easily faked from a 1000 shell, engine numbers and the model's specific fittings are the check. Hillclimb history adds real value.

generations.name: 1000 / 1000 TT / 1200 TT / TTS
generations.note: The 1000 made 43 hp, the TTs 55–65, and the TTS, with its oil cooler in the front panel, 70 hp and a competition career out of all proportion to its size.

models.intro: The Prinz grown up: a four-cylinder air-cooled saloon whose sporting derivatives, 1000 TT, 1200 TT and the twin-carburettor TTS, became the giant-killers of German hillclimbs and the car a generation of tuners (and the founders of Abt) learned on.

models.collectorNote: Engine history is everything: a Spider with a documented rotary (many were converted to piston power in period) is the real article.

generations.name: Wankel Spider
generations.note: The rotor displaced 498 cc and made 50 hp; apex-seal wear, the rotary's teething trouble, was covered by an NSU warranty generous enough to hurt.

models.intro: The first production car in the world with a Wankel rotary engine: a Bertone-bodied roadster on the Sport Prinz chassis, its single-rotor engine spinning to speeds no piston twin could match. About 2,400 were built, and every rotary Mazda descends from the bet NSU placed here.

models.collectorNote: Buy the best engine you can find, rebuilt rotaries by the small specialist circle are the difference between a driver and a project. The rest of the car is durable, refined and undervalued.

generations.name: Ro80
generations.note: Twin rotors of 497.5 cc each; the Saxomat-derived gearbox needed only a clutch touch to shift. Some 37,000 were built over ten years.

models.intro: European Car of the Year 1968 and the rotary's flagship: a twin-rotor saloon with front-wheel drive, a semi-automatic gearbox, inboard front discs and Claudio Luthe's wind-tunnel styling a decade ahead of the industry. The engine's seal problems bankrupted NSU into Volkswagen's arms, and the car itself was superb.
